title: Design an Ad Click Aggregation System
subtitle: Real-time streaming analytics, Kafka partitioning, HyperLogLog counting, and click-fraud deduplication

stages.title: Stage 1 — Direct Synchronous Database Counters
stages.bottleneck: At 50,000 ad clicks per second, `UPDATE ads SET click_count = click_count + 1 WHERE ad_id = 123` locks database rows and crashes database CPU.
stages.narrative: **Synchronous DB Increment.** Directly updating row counts in SQL for every ad click.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Kafka Ingestion & Flink Stream Window Aggregation
stages.bottleneck: Click fraud (botnets firing 10,000 clicks/sec from single IP to drain advertiser budgets).
stages.narrative: **Kafka & Flink Stream Aggregation.** Click events stream into Kafka. Apache Flink aggregates clicks into 1-minute tumbling windows in memory before writing single aggregate rows to ClickHouse.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Anti-Fraud Filter & HyperLogLog Unique User Counting
stages.bottleneck: Storing billions of unique user IDs to count unique clicks consumes massive RAM.
stages.narrative:
**Anti-Fraud & HyperLogLog.**
1. **Fraud Filter:** Rejects bot traffic based on IP click velocity rules.
2. **HyperLogLog (HLL):** Estimates unique user counts with 99% accuracy using only 12KB of memory per ad.
